crime: For several weeks, a girl brought a boxed two-player strategy game to {WITCH_NAME}'s cell each evening. They each chose their own moves, but {WITCH_NAME} politely refused help and insisted on setting up, moving both sides' pieces, and packing the game herself.

In the final week, the girl began playing with someone else in the recreation room. On the day of the murder, the girl returned to the cell, packed the remaining pieces, said the game would stay with the new partner from then on, and carried it away. When {WITCH_NAME} asked for one last private conversation in the library before lock, the girl agreed.

At 9:35 p.m., the girl placed the palm-sized metal turn marker in the box, closed it, and pasted a strip with the final score and the girl's signature over the lid seam. A prisoner at the pool table watched the girl do it. {WITCH_NAME} was not there, and neither player told her about the strip. The new partner took the sealed box to the assigned cell. From 9:45 until lock, the same witness remained beside the new partner in the shower line.

The next morning, the girl was found dead in the library. Repeated blows from a palm-sized hard object had shattered one side of her skull. {WITCH_NAME} acknowledged that they had spoken but said the girl had left alive.

The signed strip across the box was still intact. When the prisoners broke it and opened the lid, they found the metal marker inside, with the dead girl's blood and hair on its edge. The weapon appeared to have spent the night inside the new partner's locked cell, although the victim had sealed the box before the killing window and it had never been opened.

That alibi cleared the new partner. Only {WITCH_NAME} had met the victim alone and could take the marker through a closed lid and put it back. Unseen in the library, she drew it into her hand, beat the girl to death, and returned it bloodied to the box, never knowing that the lid had been sealed.
fields.epitaph: The last case to close carried only her away.
fields.epithet: The Hand That Could Not Hold On
execution: An enormous iron travel case opens in front of her. She is bound inside its narrow, shallow lower half, with the lid poised over her entire body.
The lid closes. Its rim drives her straight arms and legs inward as she strains to keep them extended. It keeps pressing, folding her knees and arms into the case and crushing her ribs.
At last the lid breaks her chest and skull, and the latch snaps shut. The case does not open again. Her corpse lies crushed and motionless inside.

magic.name: Through the Lid
magic.text: She can take an item from a sealed box or put one inside without opening it.
